figures.caption: Figure 1. Cross-subject retrieval with global soft correspondences. (a) A brain encoder trained on remaining subjects retrieves images for a held-out subject using unlabeled brain signals and a gallery, with both encoders frozen. (b) Hard landmark selection discards uncertain pairs, while independent ranking crowds a few candidates. (c) STAGE preserves soft correspondences for alignment and coordinates retrieval via shared candidate capacities. Blue circles and gold triangles denote brain and image embeddings; link widths and bars illustrate pairwise support and candidate weights.

Figure 2. The STAGE test-time adaptation pipeline. Frozen encoders map an unlabeled target batch and the gallery to neural and image embeddings. After moment calibration, global entropic soft-coupling (GES) supplies initialization weights, teacher targets for feature adaptation, and final ranking scores; only initialization and adaptation modify neural features. The coupling-matching loss guides feature alignment, while the feature anchor limits deviation from the initialized embeddings.

Figure 3. Retrieval performance with expanded galleries. Top1 over 30 subject–seed cases. Geometry is fitted without pair labels on 200 queries and 200 candidates covering their identities, then frozen for gallery expansion. Coupling, row-wise, and equalmass Sinkhorn rankings share the fitted geometry. SCORE and SATTC curves use published values; full numerical results are reported in Supplementary Table S28.

Figure 4. Qualitative retrieval comparison with SCORE. THINGS-EEG2, subject 01, seed 0, 200-image gallery. SCORE (reproduced coordinate recovery with CSLS) and STAGE share one frozen base. Each shows its top three; green borders mark the viewed image. Right: its SCORE-to-STAGE rank.

Table 1. Cross-subject retrieval accuracy (%). Above the divider, EEG2 and Alljoined use published SAMGA-based baselines from SCORE [5]; MEG uses four held-out subjects. Below it, SCORE recovery + CSLS and STAGE share frozen NICE features, queries, galleries and source seeds (0/1/2). Subject-paired intervals are reported in Supplementary Table S40.
Table 3. Progressive component ablation (Top-1/Top-5, %). The unadapted baseline and subsequent feature stages use row-wise radialdistance ranking; the last row switches to coupling ranking.

Figure 7. Effects of correspondence support, weights, and initialization rounds. THINGS-EEG2, 30 subject–seed cases, coupling ranking, no adaptation. MNN and all-pair support are compared under uniform, margin and coupling weights at K = 1 and K = 12. The hollow circle marks the degenerate all-pair fit with uniform weights.
